title: Add per-route contextual baselines and auto-quieting alert policy
author: Emily Chen
release_notes: Introduce per-route contextual baselines (latency and token cost) and an automated alert quieting policy to reduce noisy signal during traffic transitions. Adds dashboard panels and trace enrichment to surface baseline deltas.
description: Problem: Our global alert thresholds cause noisy pages for customers that have stable but different per-route behavior (e.g., long-form summarization vs short completions). Teams repeatedly tune suppression rules per-tenant which is error-prone. Goal: compute contextual baselines per-route (and per-tenant when available), expose a compact delta metric that shows deviation from expectation, and add an automated quieting policy that temporarily relaxes alert sensitivity when we detect controlled traffic transitions or known releases. Design: - Add a lightweight baseline service (telemetry/baselines) that consumes rolling aggregates (p50/p95 token_latency, token_cost_per_invocation, tokens_per_invocation) and produces a time-series of expected curves and seasonal confidence bands. - Emit new metrics: route.baseline.latency_p50, route.baseline.latency_p95, route.baseline.cost_expected, route.delta.latency_ratio, route.delta.cost_ratio, route.quiet_mode (0/1). Metrics are tagged by route, model_family, and tenant_id (when available). - Tracing enrichment: a baseline_delta_enricher attaches baseline bucket metadata and delta values to sampled traces so that traces can be filtered by 'deviation > x' in the UI. - Alerting: introduce auto_quieting policy. When a route shows a sustained deviation that matches a rollout signature (sudden global uplift with matching user-agent or release tag), the policy sets a quiet_mode flag for a short window and raises a lower-priority notification stream while still recording incidents for postmortem. - Dashboards: add per-route baseline panels (compact sparkline + baseline band) and a delta distribution heatmap to help SREs find routes with structural changes. - Backwards compatibility: baseline service only reads existing aggregates and does not change upstream telemetry. Feature is opt-in per-tenant via 'observability.features.baselines' flag. Migration & rollout: - Canary rollout in cp-west for 48 hours with observing-only mode (quiet_mode never enabled). - After validation, enable auto-quieting for internal tenants for 7 days, then customer opt-in. Testing & validation: - Unit tests for baseline windowing logic and band calculation. - Integration test simulating release surge and confirming quiet_mode toggles. - Load test for baseline service at 10k routes/sec aggregate. Observability impact: produced metrics add ~0.2 QPS per 1k routes; sampling strategy keeps cardinality bounded by route/model_family. Open items: - Decide retention window for baseline curves (default 14 days) - Add a way to bulk opt-in tenants via Linear task (ENG-4938). This PR includes implementation, dashboards, docs, tests, and rollout plan.

1) init: baseline service scaffolding and proto definitions

3) add: trace enricher and dashboard panels
4) tests: unit + integration + load harness

review_comments: Anika Patel: Left a couple of nits on naming (prefer baseline.band -> baseline.confidence_band) and asked for a note on retention sizing in the README.
Author (Emily Chen): Renamed band->confidence_band, added retention paragraph to README with default 14 days and notes about storage QPS.
Marco Ruiz: Concerned about cardinality explosion for routes with high cardinality tenant tags; requested explicit cardinality control and a fallback aggregate key.
Author (Emily Chen): Added route.cardinality_limit config with default 5k, and a fallback to route._aggregate when over limit; added tests to exercise fallback.
Jun Park: Asked that quiet_mode transitions be auditable in logs and that incidents still be recorded for postmortem (even if suppressed).
Author (Emily Chen): Added structured audit log entries (observability.baseline.quiet_mode.change) and adjusted alert policy to emit an info-level incident record while lowering pager severity.
merge_details: Merged by Marco Ruiz via squash-merge. Squash commit message: 'observability: per-route baselines + auto-quieting policy (ENG-4820) — adds baseline service, metrics, trace enrichment, dashboards, tests, docs'
notes_summary: This PR reduces paging noise for routine traffic transitions by computing per-route expectation curves and temporarily lowering alert sensitivity when deviations match rollout signatures. Opt-in by tenant; rollout plan included.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: reads existing telemetry only; added new metrics and a small service. Risk mitigations included canary, opt-in flag, and audit logs.
test_plan: Unit tests for windowing and band math, integration test for release surge signature, load test at target scale. CI runs cover unit+integration; e2e run retried once due to infra flake.
